title: Design: Pays for window with long names keeps its title, links and Close inside
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, the payer, with a long name with spaces that no other customer has, at least 60 characters (for example Northern Plains Heavy Truck and Trailer Repair Services West).
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B, whose Bill Invoices To is saved as customer A, whose name is customer A's name with every space taken out (for example NorthernPlainsHeavyTruckandTrailerRepairServicesWest).
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer C, whose Bill Invoices To is saved as customer A, with a name that no other customer has and that includes each of the characters & " ' < > (for example A&B "Fleet" O'Neil <Parts> & Sons).
  • If a name field stops before the end of a name, use the longest name it takes.
  • Open the attached picture bt-p1-18-after-pays-for-list.png at 100% zoom beside the screen.
custom_steps:
1. Open customer A's page.
  2. Click the "Pays for" counter.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The "Pays for" counter shows 2.

Step 2:

  • A window titled "[customer A's name] pays for" opens.
  • The title stays inside the window: no part of it runs past the window's edge.
  • Customer B and customer C are listed, each as a link.
  • Customer B's name stays inside its own row: no part of it covers the row under it, and that row's text can be read.
  • Customer C's name shows exactly as saved: the & " ' < > characters appear as typed, not changed into other characters or codes.
  • The line "These customers bill new work orders and part sales to [customer A's name] by default." stays inside the window.
  • The "Close" button is fully visible and nothing covers it.

Words in square brackets in a message stand for the value they name, such as customer B's name exactly as it is saved; every other word of the message must match exactly.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Bill To", Confluence 1003585538, version 0.5 (6 Nov 2026, pending approval, Chris Ward), read 9 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-12289, story SV-12303 (Story 1, Saved default Bill To on the customer page)

  • S1-R9: “Clicking the counter opens a window titled "[customer] pays for", listing each customer A to Z as a link to its page; a long list scrolls inside the window.”
  • S1-R10: “The window shows the line "These customers bill new work orders and part sales to [customer] by default." and a "Close" button.”

Design pictures attached to this case:

The design's own words:

  • “Window "A & J Truck & Trailer Repair pays for": "These customers bill new work orders and part sales to A & J Truck & Trailer Repair by default."”

The design draws this place with ordinary names only; it draws no long name without spaces and no name with & " ' < >. The stress check follows the design-case checklist (lesson L-21); the expected words come from the PRD quotes above.
